title: Implement circuit breaker + degrade-mode policy for KMS dependency
creator: Sean Gallagher
project: Security & Compliance Foundation: KMS integration hardening + rotation docs
description:
Problem
- KMS is a hard dependency for envelope decrypt + key operations. During KMS brownouts (timeouts/throttling/permission regressions), the current behavior can amplify load (retries across services) and cascade into elevated 5xx across control-plane and data-plane.
- We need a consistent circuit breaker strategy + explicit degrade-mode behavior so systems fail fast, preserve partial availability where safe, and avoid retry storms.

Goal
- Add circuit breaker behavior around KMS calls across services using the shared wrapper (ENG-4823), with policy-level guidance for what to do when the breaker is OPEN (cache-only, fail-fast, backpressure).
- Ensure behavior is observable (breaker state + short-circuit metrics) and reviewed by SRE (thresholds, paging, rollout/rollback).

Non-goals
- No new crypto primitives/algorithms.
- Not re-architecting encryption format; focus is dependency hardening + operational safety.

Proposed behavior (policy)
1) Decrypt path (read-time / request serving)
- Normal: attempt KMS decrypt (with wrapper retry budget + timeouts).
- When breaker OPEN: do not call KMS. Serve decrypt only if we can satisfy from approved cache (bounded TTL + size, keyed by ciphertext DEK hash + key id/version). Otherwise fail fast.
- Rationale: preserve availability for frequently accessed data during transient KMS events while preventing request storms.

2) Encrypt / GenerateDataKey path (write-time / key issuance)
- When breaker OPEN: fail fast (HTTP 503 / gRPC UNAVAILABLE) with actionable error including recommended operator next steps. Do not enqueue unbounded retries.
- Rationale: generating fresh DEKs requires KMS; better to shed load deterministically than to produce long tail latency and thundering herds.

3) Control-plane operations (config fetch, key metadata, rotation toggles)
- Prefer fail-fast with clear operator-facing messaging; do not block unrelated control-plane endpoints.
- For rotation/dual-read toggles: ensure we never enter a partial state due to KMS instability. If breaker OPEN, require explicit override / postpone cutover.

Circuit breaker design requirements
- Standardized implementation in the KMS wrapper so all call sites behave consistently.
- State machine: CLOSED -> OPEN -> HALF_OPEN (probe) -> CLOSED.
- Open on:
  - sustained timeouts / throttling / dependency unavailable
  - elevated error rate exceeding threshold over rolling window
- Do NOT open the breaker for:
  - AccessDenied / invalid key id / invalid ciphertext (these are configuration or correctness issues; should surface quickly and clearly)
- Half-open behavior:
  - limited probe requests per interval
  - if probe succeeds within budget, close breaker; if not, reopen.

Configuration + guardrails
- Configurable per service with safe defaults; production guardrails enforced (ENG-48502):
  - max timeout per call
  - max retry budget per request
  - max concurrent in-flight KMS calls
  - open interval / cooldown
- Explicit override required to exceed production caps.

Observability requirements (must-have)
- Metrics:
  - kms_cb_state{service,env,region} (0/1/2 or enum in logs)
  - kms_cb_open_total{reason}
  - kms_cb_short_circuit_total{operation}
  - kms_call_latency_ms{operation,outcome}
  - kms_errors_total{error_category,cloud_provider}
- Tracing:
  - span: kms.call with tags: operation, key_provider, error_category, cb_state
- Logs:
  - structured fields: kms_error_category, kms_http_status (if applicable), kms_request_id (when available), cb_state, retry_count

SRE review requirements
- SRE must sign off on:
  - open/close thresholds
  - alerting strategy (page only on sustained customer-impacting failures; ticket on noisy/intermittent)
  - rollout plan (canary + rollback triggers)
  - runbook updates (link: kms-decrypt-failures-runbook)

Acceptance criteria
- Circuit breaker integrated via shared wrapper for all KMS operations in control-plane + data-plane call sites identified in inventory.
- Breaker does not trigger on AccessDenied / InvalidCiphertext; those surface immediately with actionable error messages.
- During induced KMS outage in staging:
  - KMS call volume drops after breaker opens (no retry storm)
  - p95 request latency does not blow up due to backoffs
  - services either (a) continue reads via cache-only where applicable or (b) fail fast with 503 and clear error strings
- Dashboards include cb_state and short-circuit counts and are used during game day.

Test plan
- Unit tests for breaker state transitions and classification logic (throttle/timeout vs AccessDenied).
- Integration tests in staging harness:
  - forced timeouts
  - forced throttling
  - forced AccessDenied (ensures no breaker open)
  - verify short-circuit metrics increment and requests fail fast.

Rollout plan
- Stage 1: enable breaker with conservative thresholds in staging + canary.
- Stage 2: production canary in one region (us-east) for 24h; watch KMS latency + 5xx + cb_state.
- Stage 3: gradual rollout by service; keep feature flag for immediate rollback.

Links
- ADR-007: KMS client wrapper and failure policy (Confluence)
- Related incidents:
  - 2025-11 us-east KMS timeout spike
  - near-miss retry storm (follow-up hotfix)

Implementation notes
- Use centralized error taxonomy (ENG-4822) to classify outcomes.
- Keep cache TTL conservative to avoid serving with stale key material during rotation; coordinate with key caching changes (PR-18463) and dual-read support (PR-18478).
comments: 2025-10-16 (Sean Gallagher): Marking P0 after seeing retry amplification in staging load test. Need breaker to protect KMS and avoid cascading failures across services.
2025-10-18 (Allison Grant): Observability requirement: cb_state must be exported as a first-class metric and tagged by service/env/region; avoid per-process-only logging.

2025-10-22 (Benji Okafor): Draft implementation plan: implement breaker in wrapper; per-operation classification (Decrypt vs Encrypt vs GenerateDataKey). AccessDenied/InvalidCiphertext will bypass breaker and surface immediately.
2025-10-28 (Rafael Mendes): Please ensure breaker OPEN also reduces concurrency (max_inflight) and not just skips calls. During brownouts we still saw too many probes; keep HALF_OPEN probes bounded.
2025-11-04 (Kevin Osei): Add counters for short-circuit events + include cb_state in structured logs so on-call can correlate 5xx spikes with breaker transitions.

2025-11-08 (Sean Gallagher): SRE sign-off contingent on: (1) canary plan with rollback trigger, (2) runbook update with ‘cache-only’ behavior explained, (3) alert tuned to avoid paging on short transient KMS throttle.

2025-11-14 (Connor O'Brien): Rollout approved for prod canary after dashboards landed. Rollback trigger: sustained 5xx increase >0.5% absolute for 15m or unexpected decrypt mismatch signals during rotation window.

2025-11-22 (Benji Okafor): Merged PR-18449 + guardrails PR-18502. Verified in staging fault injection: KMS call rate drops ~90% after breaker opens; reads with cached DEKs continue for hot objects; writes fail fast with clear UNAVAILABLE + operator hint.
